Hi Neha / Marcus,

We finished a first-pass reconciliation against Brightlane's usage CSV and our raw event stream. Summary:

- Root cause: during the May 16 incident our token-aggregation worker retried a subset of ingested events while the write-ahead cache failed to de-duplicate on replay, producing duplicated token records for some sessions. Engineering has fixed the retry path and added an additional de-dup check to the aggregation pass.
- Exposure: ~12,340 duplicate tokens attributed to Brightlane across 2026-05-15T00:00:00Z -> 2026-05-16T23:59:59Z.
- Monetary impact: $248.60 in duplicate charges (attached reconciliation_DL-4827.xlsx).

Attachments: reconciliation_DL-4827.xlsx (xlsx)

Proposed next steps:
1) Issue a $248.60 credit against Invoice 2026-05-15 and send Brightlane an adjusted invoice/credit note.
2) Publish a short customer-facing explanation and link to the internal postmortem (internal postmortem contains technical detail; externally we summarize cause and mitigation).
3) Monitor for similar anomalies for the next two billing cycles and provide Brightlane with a small weekly usage report on request.

If you approve, I can draft the credit note and updated invoice and submit for finance sign-off.
